items.title: Hundreds evacuated from Russian-occupied Oleshky during rare Ukraine ceasefire
items.summary: Hundreds of people are also understood to have stayed in the front-line town, despite the dangers.
items.content:
Hundreds of residents of the devastated Russian-occupied city of Oleshky have been evacuated, Russian and Ukrainian authorities have said, following a humanitarian ceasefire brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump.

"Everything unfolded without any incidents, and both sides noted the high level of organisation," Russia's human rights ombudsman Yana Lantratova said.

Ukrainian authorities confirmed the evacuees were on their way to southern Russia, from where they will travel on to Ukraine through Belarus.

Melania Trump said that "all elements of the convoy, including the safe passageway in and out of Oleshky, was established through mutual agreement between Russian and Ukrainian leaders".

Speaking to journalists on Friday evening, Lantratova put out a joint request with her Ukrainian counterpart "to the US First Lady... that humanitarian missions such as this one, delivering aid to residents in need, be conducted on a regular basis under the coordination of Mrs Melania Trump".

A ceasefire - the longest and most widespread since the start of Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022 - has been in force in the entire frontline region of Kherson since Tuesday, allowing for the road out of Oleshky to be demined.

Residents who wished to leave had a four-hour window to do so on Friday. A convoy of 25 buses was brought in to allow up to 750 people to leave the town until 14:00 (12:00 GMT), along with ambulances for people with limited mobility.

Several hundred people are understood to have decided to stay, despite the widespread devastation and the lack of gas, electricity and running water.

"Everyone who wishes to leave Oleshky will be given the opportunity to do so safely," Ukraine's human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets said on Friday morning.

"At the same time, those who decide to remain will be able to stay and will receive all the necessary humanitarian assistance."

Ukrainian military positions lie 5km (3.1miles) from Oleshky, but the evacuees will first have to travel into Russian-occupied territory and then to the southern Russian city of Anapa.

They will board a Russian government plane to Gomel in Belarus, and then drive across the border into Ukraine's Chernihiv region.

Others are expected to choose to stay in Russian-occupied territory.

Lubinets and his Russian counterpart Yana Lantratova travelled to Oleshky together on Friday, setting off from Armiansk, in the Russian-occupied Crimean peninsula.

Lubinets is the first Ukrainian official since the start of the war to visit Russian-occupied parts of Ukraine. He will also become the first to visit Russia when he escorts the evacuees back into Ukraine on Saturday.

The Oleshky ceasefire has required close cooperation with Lantratova, which Lubinets said he carried out in the interests of saving lives.

But some in Ukraine have recoiled at the sight of him standing beside a representative of the Russian occupying power which has killed so many of the city's residents and made life unbearable for the rest.

Both Lubinets and Lantratova posted videos from Oleshky on their social media channels, saying people were given the chance to form two groups depending on whether they wanted to be taken to Russian-controlled territory or to Ukraine.

In one video, Lubinets can be seen meeting tearful locals. "The problem is that a lot of people are staying," he can be heard saying. "I was told that it was their own choice, we will do everything possible for the humanitarian aid to arrive."

Russia said on Thursday that it had prepared "dozens of tonnes" of aid for the residents who do not wish to leave, including food, medicine, hygiene products and fuel for generators.

An Oleshky resident told the BBC she had decided against leaving because "they wouldn't take my animals, so that's it."

Olena, who now lives in Kyiv, said her grandmother and wider family in Oleshky were also staying behind.

"The older generation does not want to leave," she told the BBC. "I've barely managed to persuade my father - and only because I've just had a baby, who he would never see otherwise."

"She lost her legs after stepping on a landmine, covered in snow... People took her to the hospital in a garden wheelbarrow," Olena said.

"That's how locals transport all wounded and dead people in Oleshky to the hospital and the hospital's morgue: in garden wheelbarrows."

The ceasefire is due to be in force until the end of Sunday 1 November. It has provided the first few days of peace in the Kherson region since the start of Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

Residents of Kherson told the BBC they were "overjoyed" by the ceasefire. However, they are concerned the truce has given Russia time to build up its military presence on the banks of the Dnipro river, which could result in a renewed assault once the ceasefire expires.

On Friday, the Kremlin made it clear that the success of the Oleshky ceasefire should not be interpreted as willingness to extend the truce to the rest of Ukraine.

A handful of foreign journalists have been invited to witness the evacuation of the town, which Moscow is expected to present as a humanitarian mission conducted with mercy to protect the people of Oleshky.

Many Ukrainians suspect Russia's real intention is to earn credit with the White House, and to provide US President Donald Trump with a boost ahead of next week's midterm elections.

items.title: MacBook Pro touchscreen verso gli 1,5 milioni di modelli venduti entro il 2027?

items.content:
Tra 1,2 e 1,5 milioni di unità nel 2027, è quanto potrebbe vendere Apple con il nuovo MacBook Pro OLED secondo i calcoli di TrendForce. La previsione riguarda chiaramente un prodotto molto costoso, bisogna considerarlo, ma è altresì vero che quest'ultimo potrebbe avere effetti anche su un mercato finora dominato dai produttori di PC Windows.

Il listino parte da 2.899 dollari negli USA per il modello da 14 pollici. Per il 16 pollici bisogna invece mettere in conto almeno 3.399 dollari. Non sono certo somme da acquisto impulsivo, soprattutto perché i MacBook Pro con schermo mini-LED continuano ad essere disponibili, ed ovviamente ci sono anche gli altri modelli ancora in vendita. TrendForce considera proprio il prezzo uno dei possibili freni alle vendite nella prima fase, quando una parte dei clienti potrebbe preferire aspettare prima di cambiare laptop.

items.title: Strage di Castel D'Azzano, tre carabinieri indagati per omicidio colposo
items.summary: Il fascicolo è stato aperto dalla Procura di Verona
items.content:
Tre carabinieri sono indagati per concorso in omicidio colposo plurimo dalla procura di Verona. Si tratta dei tre militari, tutti comandanti, che erano responsabili dell'operazione per lo sgombero del casolare dei fratelli Ramponi , a Castel d'Azzano nel Veronese, il 14 ottobre del 2025.

L’operazione finì in tragedia con la morte di tre carabinieri. I nomi dei tre indagati sono emersi durante l'udienza per il procedimento disciplinare su cui indaga la procura generale di Venezia che è stato avviato sempre nei confronti dei tre comandanti. Al centro delle contestazioni ci sono presunte negligenze nella pianificazione e nella conduzione del blitz, compresa la decisione di proseguire l'intervento nonostante i segnali di pericolo, tra cui la presenza di gas nell'edificio. I tre indagati sono il comandante della compagnia di Villafranca Vincenzo Spataro , il tenente colonnello Antonio Sframeli , allora comandante del reparto operativo, e il colonnello Claudio Papagno , comandante provinciale dei carabinieri di Verona.

L’udienza per il procedimento disciplinare è stata sospesa proprio perché i tre militari «sono già indagati» a Verona. La richiesta è stata ufficializzata venerdì alla Corte d'Appello di Venezia dall'avvocato Gianfranco Ceoletta , che difende i tre comandanti e contro cui la procuratrice generale Paola Tonini , affiancata dall'avvocato generale Nicola Proto , si è opposta. Per l’accusa si tratta di «percorsi paralleli che non si sovrappongono».

items.content:
Lo sapevate che Stati Uniti e Giappone controllano il mercato dei microscopi più avanzati? Questo perché, banalmente, sono in grado di produrre i modelli più potenti, ma la cose stanno per cambiare. O meglio, un nuovo player sta per aggiungersi, ed è facile intuire chi.

Parliamo in questo caso di microscopi elettronici, strumenti indispensabili non soltanto per l'industria dei chip, ma anche per la ricerca sui nuovi materiali e sulle strutture biologiche. E se per anni, il mercato di questi apparecchi è rimasto concentrato nelle mani di pochi produttori, ora la Cina sta cercando di cambiare la situazione, sviluppando strumenti scientifici nazionali capaci di competere con quelli occidentali.

Un passo importante arriva dal TEM-F200, un microscopio elettronico a trasmissione da 200 kV sviluppato dalla cinese CIQTEK e presentato il 18 ottobre durante la conferenza nazionale di microscopia elettronica a Nanchino. items.summary: NIU svela a EICMA la gamma scooter 2027: debutta l'ammiraglia FQiX 500 da 115 km/h e autonomia fino a 130 km, insieme a 25 novità per i modelli NQi, NQiX e FQiX.
items.content:
I riflettori di EICMA sono pronti ad accendersi i fari sono puntati anche sulla nuova linea di ciclomotori e scooter firmata NIU per il 2027. La casa asiatica approda a Milano con una doppia novità: da un lato il debutto della FQiX 500, destinata a posizionarsi al vertice dell'offerta, dall'altro un pacchetto di ben 25 affinamenti tecnici e strutturali distribuiti tra le famiglie NQi, NQiX e FQiX.

FQiX 500: prestazioni, ABS e tripla batteria

Sviluppato partendo dall'architettura della NQiX 500, il nuovo FQiX 500 ne eredita il telaio rinforzato per rileggerlo secondo i tratti stilistici propri della serie FQiX. Il risultato è il modello più prestazionale della gamma, capace di raggiungere i 110 km/h di velocità massima e di spingersi fino a 115 km/h in modalità Boost, mantenendo l'ABS di serie.L'alimentazione si affida di base a due batterie da 72V / 28 Ah, ma la vera novità risiede nello spazio ricavato sotto la sella: qui è possibile installare un terzo accumulatore opzionale che porta l'autonomia complessiva fino a 130 chilometri. Il debutto nelle concessionarie europee è previsto nel primo trimestre del 2027. Prezzo d'attacco fissato a 4.699 euro.

Gamma MY27: 25 interventi tra telaio, batterie e dotazioni

Il resto del catalogo 2027 beneficia di un aggiornamento diffuso che tocca ciclistica, elettronica e accumulatori. La NQiX 500 adotta ora uno scheletro in acciaio ad alta resistenza HC420 e alza la propria velocità di punta da 100 a 110 km/h (115 km/h in Boost). Mentre sui modelli NQiX 150/300, FQiX 150/300 e sulla coppia NQi Sport/GTS debutta invece un nuovo pacco batterie compatto da 72V / 30 Ah, in grado di garantire fino al 7% di autonomia in più.Il nuovo modulo condivide lo stesso caricabatterie ed è totalmente retrocompatibile con i veicoli delle annate MY25 e MY26. La sicurezza di marcia passa per l'adozione di serie degli pneumatici all-season CST SC12 su tutta la gamma, affiancati da fari anteriori più potenti per le linee NQiX e FQiX. A completare il restyling intervengono un modulo GPS più rapido, un trattamento anticorrosione potenziato per telai, cavalletti e forcelloni, oltre alle tre nuove colorazioni Matt Blue, Jungle Green e Nardo Grey riservate alla serie NQiX. L'arrivo sul mercato di tutti i veicoli aggiornati è programmato per il primo trimestre del 2027.

items.title: AI isn't replacing SREs, it's deskilling them
items.summary: Article URL: https://newsletter.signoz.io/p/ai-isnt-replacing-sres-its-deskilling Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50305693 Points: 359 # Comments: 283
items.content:
This newsletter is a n honest attempt to talk about all things - observability, OpenTelemetry, open-source and the engineering in between! & This piece took 6 days, 5 hours to be cooked, hope we served. 🌚

There are two popular prophecies floating around tech circles these days.

The first says SRE is the future of all software engineering , that as AI writes more and more code, the humans who remain will be the ones keeping systems alive. The second says AI will devour every tech job alive, SREs included. Neither is particularly useful if you’re an SRE trying to figure out what your Tuesday will look like in 2027.

Let’s ask a more grounded question by looking at what’s already happening: When AI handles 95% of your incident response, do you get worse at handling the 5% that actually matters?

Most of us already use AI for our daily work (our brains a little fried!), and so do SREs. Today’s discussion agenda is not whether AI replaces SREs, but whether AI is quietly making SREs less capable and whether anyone will notice anything before the next novel outage hits. The foundational framework for this entire debate comes from a 1983 research paper that’s eerily prescient.

Note from author: Below is a brief precursor to History of Automation, which you might enjoy if you are into History and Cultures (like me 😉).

In 1983, a cognitive psychologist named Lisanne Bainbridge published a paper called Ironies of Automation . It became one of the most cited papers in human factors research, and its core argument is almost uncomfortably relevant today.

Bainbridge studied what happened when factories and industrial systems automated the work of blue-collar operators. The findings were paradoxical and revealed that the more you automate a process, the more critical the human operator becomes during the rare moments automation fails and the less practice they get, and the worse they become at exactly those interventions. Automation, which was inherently designed to remove humans from the loop, left them with the worst possible job, i.e., long stretches of passive monitoring punctuated by rare, high-stakes crises they were increasingly unprepared for.

Basically, I’m drawing a parallel between the AI revolution and industrial automation. Industrial automation reshaped blue-collar work by taking over routine physical tasks, and the workers who remained had to handle exceptions they’d lost the muscle memory for. AI is doing the same thing to knowledge workers by taking over the routine cognitive tasks, the pattern matching, the triage, the known-issue resolution and leaving humans with the rare, complex, ambiguous problems.

The exact problems that require deep expertise , the exact expertise that atrophies when you stop practising.

Now we’re replaying this pattern with AI agents, and the stakes in software systems are only growing.

Let’s take stock of where things stand today in the world of site reliability engineering.

Alert noise reduction and intelligent grouping, runbook execution for known issues, log pattern detection and anomaly flagging, and basic root-cause suggestions from historical incident data, and auto-remediation for well-understood failure modes like restarting a crashed pod or scaling up a service that’s running hot, are all fairly automated today.

Some immediate targets include multi-signal correlation across metrics, logs, and traces, autonomous root-cause analysis for partially understood failures, predictive incident detection before users are affected, AI-driven change risk assessment and automated rollbacks.

Tier 1 incidents: Known issues with known fixes get fully automated.

Tier 2 incidents: Partially understood problems receive AI recommendations with human validation.

Tier 3 incidents: Novel, complex, cascading failures stay human-led, with AI providing supporting context.

If human SREs (okay, now we have to use adjectives like human 🥹) only engage with Tier 3 incidents, i.e. the novel, never-before-seen outages, where do they build the intuition to handle them? Intuition is usually developed from years of hands-on incident response, pattern recognition built through repetition, and the kind of gut-level understanding of a system that only develops from painfully waking up at the odd hour to solve the bug that brought the system down.

Subscribe if you wish to read some more hot takes. We are cooking some great ones!

This is where the picture starts getting blurry. Let’s look at some emerging research on AI-induced deskilling across multiple fields, which paints a consistent and concerning picture.

In medicine, a recent study found that endoscopists who used AI assistance for polyp detection saw their unassisted detection rates drop from 28% to 22% after a period of AI use. They got worse at the thing they were supposed to be experts in, not because they forgot the theory, but because they stopped exercising the skill.

In aviation, research has shown that long-haul pilots who rely heavily on autopilot systems experience measurable degradation in situational awareness and manual flying ability. The problem got serious enough that the FAA now mandates more manual flying time to counteract the effect.

Somewhere over the past year, AI stopped being a tool I occasionally reached for and became the first thing I reach for, always . My instinct now is to offload as much as possible and apply my own thinking only where it’s absolutely unavoidable. The problem is that these moments are becoming the only exercises my brain gets, and I can feel the rust .

We can draw a pattern here. The more you let the system handle, the worse you get at handling things yourself and here’s the truly dangerous part, you don’t feel it happening . It gets masked as hyper-productivity. Cognitive research suggests that because AI tools make tasks feel easier and enhance visible performance, users are often unable to accurately judge the true status of their own skills. You feel competent, dashboards look green, and then on a Wednesday, a novel incident hits that doesn’t match any pattern the AI has seen, and you realise the muscle has atrophied.

For SREs, this manifests in specific ways, like we stop reading raw log streams because the AI summarises them, we stop forming hypotheses during incidents because the AI suggests root causes, we stop building mental models of system architecture because the AI maps dependencies for us, and each of these individually looks like a productivity win. Collectively, they hollow out the very expertise that makes an SRE effective when things go sideways in ways nobody anticipated.

But there’s something even more concerning than deskilling, and researchers have started calling it never-skilling . Deskilling means you once had a capability but have since lost it. Never-skilling means you never developed it in the first place. For junior SREs entering the field today in an environment where AI handles most of the incident response workflow, the opportunities to build foundational intuition and muscle through hands-on practice are vanishing.

The training pipeline itself is broken and not self-healing .

SREs realise their skills are degrading and lean more on AI to compensate, which further degrades their skills, creating a vicious cycle from which escape is difficult.

We are definitely not rejecting AI tooling; we are adopting it and integrating it stronger than ever before, because that’s the only way forward.

Deliberate inefficiency. Just as the FAA mandates manual flying time even when the autopilot is perfectly capable, SRE teams can designate certain incidents, even the ones the AI could handle, as human-practice opportunities . This can be considered as a long-term investment to keep skills fresh, although it might come at the cost of a super-fast solution

Build for human-in-the-loop, not human-on-the-side. There’s a meaningful difference between a system where a human approves an AI’s recommendation and one where a human actively engages with the problem alongside AI. The former keeps humans in a supervisory role that Bainbridge (the lady who wrote that research paper about 40 years ago) showed leads to vigilance decay, and the latter keeps them cognitively engaged.

Everything we’ve discussed here, the ironies of automation, the deskilling risk, the never-skilling problem, collectively applies well beyond SRE. Software engineering as a whole is navigating the same tension. As AI writes more code, reviews more PRs, and handles more debugging, the same questions apply.

We’re talking about SREs specifically because that’s the world we live in at SigNoz . We build an open-source observability platform, the kind of tool that gives SREs the metrics, traces, and logs they need to understand their systems deeply. For us, this deskilling question is not a rhetorical fad; it directly shapes how we’re building AI into our product.

Our approach is to start with an AI assistant that helps SREs leverage the power of LLMs while keeping humans firmly in control. Eventually, we’ll enable more autonomy but within clear guardrails, and only as trust is earned.

items.title: Toyota bZ4X diventa un robotaxi in Giappone. Nel 2027 i test con Waymo
items.summary: Prima i test di validazione nel 2027 in Giappone, poi "negli anni successivi" il debutto nel Regno Unito e altri mercati ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Dopo 18 mesi di intese preliminari, Toyota e Waymo passano ai fatti. Nel 2027 partirà in Giappone la sperimentazione di una flotta di Toyota bZ4X a guida autonoma . Il Regno Unito e gli altri mercati seguiranno “negli anni successivi”, senza date precise.

Le auto nasceranno nello stabilimento Toyota di Takaoka, a Toyota City (prefettura di Aichi). Dalla scocca fino all’installazione dell’hardware Waymo, tutto avviene nello stesso sito , senza modifiche fatte in un secondo momento. Il livello di guida è il 4, cioè nessun conducente a bordo in condizioni definite. Per i passeggeri sono previsti più spazio dietro, porte automatiche, portellone elettrico e luci d’ambiente.

Giappone e Regno Unito guidano a sinistra e la bZ4X di Takaoka è prodotta con volante a destra. Il vicepresidente esecutivo di Toyota, Kazuki Nakajima, ha aggiunto che esiste anche la versione a guida a sinistra, ma l’azienda vuole prima fare esperienza in Giappone.

Il 2027 è l’anno dei test e della validazione, non del servizio commerciale. Il servizio vero e proprio a Tokyo è un progetto parallelo di Waymo con Nihon Kotsu e GO, previsto sempre per il 2027 e subordinato alle approvazioni. Oggi Waymo usa Jaguar I-Pace. A Londra le prove vanno avanti da mesi e si aspettano i permessi.

Toyota e Waymo dicono che continueranno a studiare la tecnologia anche per le Toyota di proprietà . Insieme con Woven by Toyota, sussidiaria del gruppo Toyota focalizzata sui sistemi di guida autonoma, le due società vogliono capire come i dati raccolti sulle strade possano aiutare anche gli altri utenti della strada.

Toyota non sviluppa la guida autonoma da sola e s i affida a partner diversi per ogni area. In Cina c’è Pony.ai, con robotaxi basati sempre sulla bZ4X e oltre 1.000 unità previste nel 2026. In Giappone c’è Tier IV, per portare la guida autonoma di livello 4 sul minibus e-Palette entro il 2027. Negli Stati Uniti, oltre a Waymo, c’è May Mobility.

La concorrenza non sta a guardare: Nissan prepara a Tokyo un progetto con Wayve e Uber, sempre per il 2027 e per ora con operatori di sicurezza a bordo.

items.title: Florilegium: Procedural Flowers in LaTeX
items.summary: Article URL: https://github.com/kevinraymond/florilegium Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50305637 Points: 126 # Comments: 22
items.content:
The Reddit post asked how to make flowers like these in LaTeX. I don't know how the original was made, and this project doesn't try to reproduce it. It is one possible way, and the way I did it: hand-authored primitives with randomized parameters, painted in Lua, placed by a procedural layout whose "fill the unused space" part borrows a 1998 idea from the ornament literature. It gets a similar look.

Procedurally generated Delft-blue floral page margins for LaTeX. No images, no imported paths, no external assets: every petal, leaf and stem is a parametric curve computed in Lua while the page is being written, painted like a watercolor, and written straight into the PDF. Every page gets its own garden.

Six seeds of the grown composition. Same code, different seed — and the garden fills whatever space the text leaves free.

Two documents share one package, and a third shows what else it does:

Both PDFs are self-describing: the body text is the write-up of how the margin is drawn.

Last page of the grown document: the text ends early, so branches arch into the space below.

300 dpi crop. Mottled washes with white streaks lifted out, lobed leaves with white veins, forget-me-not cymes, a pale ghost flower behind the stems.

Seed 6, from an empty margin to the finished page. The stems rise first, leaves open as the tips pass their nodes, and each stem ends in a flower. Then the greedy loop takes over: on the right, each dashed circle is the largest free disc it found, just before a branch grows to it. Big holes come first and slowly, small ones last and fast. The butterflies and bees fly in, the bird glides onto its twig, and the snail crawls up its stem until the last frame, which is exactly the page this seed always gives.

The growth is recorded once, while the page is laid out: each stem is also drawn as prefixes of increasing length and each motif at a few smaller scales, replaying the same random draws. A frame then writes the pieces whose time has come, in their original painting order. make grow-6 renders one seed this way ( build/grow-6.gif and .mp4 , about 45 seconds); add EXPLAIN=1 for the dashed circles.

showcase.tex , "A year in the margin": spring on the first page, summer, autumn on the last. Each section describes the feature it shows.

One seed in spring, early summer, late summer and autumn. The seasons change what grows, not where.

Most pages have visitors: a butterfly or two and bees in the open spaces, a snail crawling up one of the main stems, and on about one page in five a bird perched on a twig of its own. They come from a random stream of their own, so a page without them is exactly the page it would have been; the option novisitors leaves them out.

The whole palette comes from one color, ink : Delft blue, sepia, green, crimson, violet, teal. The ramp from the darkest stroke to the palest wash is computed from that hue in OKLCH, so the light end never turns gray.

postscript/florilegium.ps : the grown margin in pure PostScript, one self-contained file. Ghostscript, or a printer, computes every petal while it interprets the page, and the two pages of text explain how.

The drawing core, every primitive and the growth loop are ported from ink.lua , flora.lua and grow.lua , procedure for procedure. It needs no TeX and no other file:

-dSeed=N picks the garden; without it the clock picks one, so every print is new. -dAge=0 to 1 sets the season, and -dNoVisitors leaves out the butterflies, bees, snail and bird. Two pages take about 2.5 seconds. Much of the Lua maps directly: PostScript's own transformation matrix places each primitive (translate, rotate, scale), paths and Bézier curves are native, and procedures built at run time stand in for Lua's closures (a petal's half-width is a procedure handed to the outline builder). Four things don't map:

The file sent twice to an Epson inkjet with lp postscript/florilegium.ps , with no seed given. The computer's print system runs the program again for each job, so each print takes its seed from the clock and grows a different garden. A printer gets the opaque version, as it has no transparency.

LuaLaTeX, one pass, about a second a page (two passes for showcase.tex , whose seasons need the page count).

No TeX installed? Build the image once and run everything in it:

Or paste florilegium.sty , the six .lua files and one of the .tex files into an Overleaf project and set the compiler to LuaLaTeX.

A fixed seed instead of the page number: lualatex "\def\florilegiumseed{7}\input{florilegium-grow.tex}" .

Any primitive can be drawn on its own inside a TikZ picture, under the current scope's shift, rotation and scale:

Drawing ( ink.lua ). All geometry is computed in Lua and written as PDF path operators into one literal node per page; TeX does no arithmetic. Primitives are drawn in a local frame under an affine transform, which is read from TikZ when a primitive is called inside a scope. Colors come from a tone ramp derived from the one document color ink : navy to mist at the hue of ink , interpolated in OKLCH so the light end stays blue instead of turning gray. Tapered strokes are two offset Béziers, not sampled ribbons.

Primitives ( flora.lua ). Painted in the order a watercolorist would: a flat wash, darker blotches multiplied over it, pigment pooling at the edges, streaks lifted out in white, a few fine veins, and almost no outlines. Broad petals and flowers, star lilies seen at a tilt, blossoms and florets, buds and bellflowers; lobed and entire leaves; forget-me-not cymes that curl like a scorpion's tail, branching sprigs, umbels, tendrils, seed heads; butterflies, bees, snails and a bird; copper sparkles, rosettes and the ivy-leaf fleuron whose stem becomes the head rule. Any of them can be painted as a pale ghost.

Authored composition ( authored.lua ). A plant grows from a root in the bottom-left corner: three stems through hand-picked control points, a fourth along the bottom of the page as the footer, leaves at chosen fractions of the stems, and every other motif on a branch that leaves its stem tangentially and arrives along the motif's axis — so every flower can be traced back to the root.

Grown composition ( grow.lua ), in the spirit of Wong, Zongker & Salesin, Computer-Generated Floral Ornament (SIGGRAPH 1998). The stems sway up the column as smooth noise of their height; leaves are hung at their nodes where there is room. Then, repeatedly: take the largest free disc within reach of a stem, choose a motif that fits it, and grow a branch to it from the nearest stem point; the branch becomes a stem in turn. Big holes are taken first, so flowers and lilies land early, sprays and leaves fill the middle, and the loop ends by tucking leaflets, buds and florets onto the stems. The end of the text is measured with \pagetotal in the same pass, so a short last page grows branches into the space below it with one compilation.

Reading the page ( florilegium.lua ). A heading or \florilegiumbloom leaves an invisible marker node in the text. When the page is shipped out, its box is walked node by node, adding up heights, depths and the glue as it was set, to find each marker's height on the page; the garden then gives those lines their flowers before any leaf is hung. An age reweights the motifs: buds and sprays of buds in spring, seed heads in autumn, when some leaves are painted with a ramp built from the accent instead of the ink.

Initials ( initial.lua ). The letter's outline comes from luaotfload's OpenType reader as Bézier segments. Flattened into polygons, it gives an even-odd inside test, and a grid of distances to the letter and the frame finds the largest gaps for the flowers. The vine is a Catmull-Rom curve across the tile; where it crosses the letter it goes over and under in turn, and the strands that go over are drawn again, clipped to the letter, with a thin halo of paper.

Procedural ≠ random. The seed is derived from the page number, so page n always gets garden n . Reproducibility is what makes the document stable enough to typeset.

See CLAUDE.md for a handoff-style map of the code, the tunables, and ideas not yet done.

items.summary: È il piano Base con pubblicità, e si potrà attivare dal mese prossimo.
items.content:
Su DAZN è in arrivo HBO Max, e senza sovrapprezzi - almeno per quanto riguarda il piano Base con pubblicità. La novità debutterà a novembre e riguarderà DAZN Family; la piattaforma aveva già stretto una partnership con il colosso Skydance, che ricordiamo da poco comprende sia Paramount sia Warner Bros. Discovery, grazie alla quale aveva incluso nella sua offerta alcuni canali del gruppo, tra cui Nove, Real Time, DMAX e Discovery.

Il nuovo accordo è un'espansione, in ultimo, ma davvero massiccia, tramite la quale DAZN ora include un vero e proprio servizio di streaming di film e serie TV, peraltro uno con un catalogo ricchissimo di produzioni apprezzatissime in tutto il mondo. Game of Thrones incluso, naturalmente; ma è oggettivamente solo la punta dell'iceberg. Da notare che la promozione interesserà sia chi sottoscrive un nuovo abbonamento da DAZN Family a partire dal mese prossimo sia chi ce l'ha già attivo.

Le condizioni dell'offerta di HBO sono relativamente modeste: la risoluzione massima è FHD 1080p, il numero di dispositivi che possono accedere in contemporanea si ferma a due, e naturalmente sono previste interruzioni pubblicitarie durante film e serie TV. La promozione rimarrà attiva per tutta la durata dell'abbonamento DAZN Family, senza richiedere un pagamento aggiuntivo per HBO Max. Attenzione, però: l'offerta va attivata manualmente, dirigendosi nell'area personale del proprio account DAZN e selezionando il banner dedicato, che li reindirizzerà alla procedura di attivazione su HBO Max. Analogamente, i contenuti non saranno riprodotti direttamente da DAZN: servirà l'app ufficiale di HBO Max. I due account rimarranno separati.

items.title: The federated code forge
items.summary: Article URL: https://tangled.org/blog/forge/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50305573 Points: 142 # Comments: 52
items.content:
For most of the past two decades, the code forge has been where projects live: where code is hosted, where changes are reviewed, and where contributors find each other. Forges offered convenience in exchange for centralisation.

But the centralised forge is crumbling. Relying on someone else for uptime, for features, and to be a good steward of your code hasn’t played out well. What has stood the test of time is email: Git to move the code, and email — an open protocol — to talk about it. At the cost of user experience, however.

Tangled aims to give you the best of both: the longevity of an open protocol, with the convenience and polish of a proper forge.

It’s the first truly federated code forge — you can host code on your own servers and still collaborate seamlessly with others. Our approach is pragmatic: self-host just the parts you want, like Git hosting or CI runners, or all of it, including the API server and UI. Whatever you choose , you can still talk to everyone else.

Owning your infrastructure also means you can hack on, extend and customise your forge as you see fit. Because Tangled is built on the AT Protocol, you can build your own extensions, subscribe to the firehose, or even write entirely custom knots, like this one that runs on Cloudflare Workers and uses their Artifacts product for git storage. Or an entirely custom spindle such as mitchellh.com/tack . Go even further and host our ultralight API server and build your own custom forge.

Agents have made building such hyper-personalized software trivial, and especially so when software is designed with hackability in mind from the get-go. Tangled is incredibly agent friendly .

The future of software engineering may be a moving target, but our bets on open protocols and developer agency give us the agility to move with it, and to become y o u r c o d e f o r g e f o r t h e n e x t d e c a d e .

The obvious big one: with this release, Tangled has a whole new look. We’ve redone the UI on top of our new architecture (described further below), in Svelte. Things should now be quicker, visually consistent and prettier! The keen eyed of you might’ve also spotted that we’ve swapped out Inter for Timeless Sans .

Until now, Tangled’s web UI and backend were a single Go monolith called the appview . The appview service handled AT Protocol indexing, caching, off-protocol data and UI rendering using html/template + htmx. It ran on a single SQLite database on one medium-sized server in Sweden.

This was great as long as you were ~50–100 ms away from Sweden, but most of our users aren’t! We rearchitected: we built a new standalone frontend app in Svelte, deployed at the edge. It is populated by our new diskless, entirely in-memory indexer service written in Rust: bobbin . Bobbins are deployed globally in over 11+ regions, ensuring users around the world get the best API and UI performance.

The astute reader might’ve noticed: bobbin is purely read-only and only deals with AT Protocol data. What of the rest? That functionality (and more) has been delegated to a new set of supporting services.

First, the data model itself: we have a new set of lexicons, and everything now lives under org.tangled.* , replacing the old sh.tangled.* records.

Knot2 is our aptly named, second implementation of the knot server, this time rewritten in Rust. Knot2 bakes a fully custom Git server, and also bundles in an SSH server in the same binary.

With knot2, we’ve also changed where some of that data lives. Issues, pull requests, comments, reactions and labels are now stored on the knot, right next to the code, as collaborative objects (COBs). A COB is just a chain of Git objects in the repo itself. Collaborators, knot members and the blocklist are also stored the same way.

In that sense, knots now behave a lot like a PDS: they hold signed records, full history included, for everything that belongs to a repo and much like a PDS, these records are synced via the standard AT Protocol firehose.

But why? A project’s issues and pull requests are as much a part of it as its code, so they should live with it, wherever you choose to host it. This gives your project maximum portability.

If the knot writes your issues and comments, what stops it from putting words in your mouth? Attestations. Every time you create or edit a record on a knot, the web app also writes an org.tangled.graph.attestation record to your own PDS, pointing at that exact version of the record and the COB change behind it. Two-way verification!

Self-hosters will have to upgrade their knots to the v1.20.0 by following the upgrade guide .

Organization accounts are here! An Organization on Tangled is a real AT Protocol account, with its own DID and handle, hosted on a Tranquil PDS instance. They’re passwordless, delegated accounts: you create one from the New Organization page, and you get .tngl.sh with yourself as its owner. Owners can invite members, and anyone in the Organization can act as it when creating or forking repositories. Like any other account, you can swap the handle out for a domain you own. If you’ve been running a regular account as a stand-in “org”, hang tight — we’re working on a way to move those over. Read more in the docs .

Our PR flow has been overhauled. The new flow gives everyone, regardless of whether you use Jujutsu or just vanilla Git, the ability to submit and review stacked PRs. If you’re using Git, you now get the ability to interdiff between versions (previously called rounds). JJ users get to interdiff between individual changes as well.

This isn’t all. We’re staggering this launch across the next few weeks. Up next are private repos, a CLI, SDKs for different languages and skills for your agent.

items.title: Blockchain intelligence firms link North Korea to $6.3B hack on Binance
items.summary: Article URL: https://www.npr.org/2026/10/30/g-s1-150902/blockchain-intelligence-firms-link-north-korea-to-6-3b-hack-on-binance Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50305480 Points: 142 # Comments: 87
items.content:
FILE - The Binance logo is seen on a smartphone, Feb. 28, 2023, in Marple Township, Pa. Matt Slocum/AP hide caption

A U.S.-based blockchain intelligence firm says a North Korean unit was likely behind the hack that impacted more than $6 billion on Binance, the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange.

Binance said it worked with blockchain partners to freeze roughly $3 billion in affected assets. It said Friday that it was beginning to recover assets for users.

The cryptocurrency exchange said deposits were unaffected, while withdrawals have been suspended and are expected to resume in the next day or two. It said it will cover all losses.

The company said on X that an initial investigation suggested the incident may have involved a compromised laptop, but that a subsequent investigation uncovered additional "points of breach."

TRM, in a post on its website Thursday, attributed the attack to TraderTraitor, which it described as North Korea's elite hacking unit. "We make this judgment with high confidence," the firm said.

"An attacker moved approximately USD 6.36 billion out of Binance wallets on ten blockchains, most of it in about 20 minutes," TRM said. That would make the hack the largest cryptocurrency theft on record, it said.

In February last year, another cryptocurrency exchange, Bybit, suffered a $1.5 billion hit when it was hacked. The FBI said North Korea and TraderTraitor were responsible for the hack.

"Several features of this attack match earlier North Korea-linked heists, including the Bybit hack," TRM said.

Blockchain analysis company Chainalysis also believed the Binance hack was "likely done by DPRK group TraderTraitor," its co-founder and CEO Jonathan Levin wrote on X. DPRK stands for the Democratic People's Republic of Korea, North Korea's official name.

Asked about the potential ties to North Korea, a Binance spokesperson said only that the company is "working closely with our law enforcement partners to confirm the identity of the criminals and bring them to justice."

Experts say North Korea has turned to crypto hacking and other illicit cyber activities as a source of badly needed foreign currency to support its troubled economy and fund its nuclear program in the wake of tough U.N. sanctions and other difficulties.

In December 2022, South Korea's spy agency said North Korean hackers had stolen an estimated 1.5 trillion won ($1.1 billion) in cryptocurrency and other virtual assets in the past five years, more than half of it in 2022 alone. It said North Korea's capacity to steal digital assets was considered among the best in the world.

Changpeng Zhao, also known as CZ, founded Binance in 2017. In 2023, he pleaded guilty to a felony linked to failing to prevent money laundering on the platform, and stepped down as the company's CEO. U.S. President Donald Trump pardoned Zhao in 2025.

Zhao posted Thursday on X that "User funds are safe!" but added that the theft "does look like a hack on Binance." He added that while he doesn't manage Binance anymore, "as a shareholder, I expect all user funds will be fully covered."

The event, meanwhile, also raises questions about why stronger approval controls were not in place, said Kok Tin Gan, cofounder and CEO of cybersecurity firm NyxLab.

"This looks like one signature that gave the attacker a never-expiring, full-access token to a Binance hot wallet," he said, referring to cryptocurrency wallets that hold users' "private keys," or unique authorizations, digitally and which are connected to the internet.

Binance said on X it had "found no evidence of any wallet private key leak" and that the company would release more technical details when its probe is complete.

items.summary: Chi ha o sottoscrive il piano Family di DAZN potrà attivare HBO Max Base con pubblicità nei prossimi giorni. L'accesso alla piattaforma di streaming di Skydance resterà attivo fino a quando si continua a pagare DAZN. ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
La mossa si inserisce in un percorso già avviato di collaborazione tra DAZN e Warner Bros. Discovery, iniziato con l’arrivo in app dei canali Nove, Real Time, DMAX e Discovery.

L’offerta vale solo per chi è abbonato direttamente a DAZN tramite DAZN, sia con piani annuali (in un’unica soluzione o dilazionati in 12 mesi) sia mensili; resta escluso quindi chi ha DAZN tramite TIMVISION, anche con piano Family: per loro bisogna rivolgersi a TIM, che ha già pacchetti con DAZN e HBO Max.

Il collegamento tra HBO Max e DAZN è legato da un vincolo strettissimo: se si disdice il Family, si passa a un altro piano o si esercita il recesso l'account HBO Max incluso viene disattivato anche se non cancellato. Se si mette in pausa DAZN, la pausa vale anche per HBO Max. Se si lascia il Family e si torna dopo, l’attivazione non è automatica e va rifatta.

items.title: Fiat Topolino, ora può circolare sulle strade USA e arriva l'esemplare Sanlorenzo
items.summary: Fiat Topolino 2027 ottiene l'omologazione stradale negli USA come Low-Speed Vehicle. Arrivano nuovi colori, la Open Air e un esemplare speciale Sanlorenzo
items.content:
La Fiat Topolino conquista una nuova libertà negli Stati Uniti. La microcar, già commercializzata oltreoceano, può adesso circolare legalmente sulle strade pubbliche americane grazie all'omologazione come Low-Speed Vehicle (LSV). Una novità che ne amplia concretamente le possibilità di utilizzo, trasformandola da mezzo destinato prevalentemente ad aree private a soluzione per gli spostamenti quotidiani nei contesti urbani consentiti.Il cambiamento accompagna il lancio della gamma 2027, caratterizzata da nuove colorazioni, una variante Open Air e un esemplare esclusivo realizzato insieme al cantiere nautico Sanlorenzo. Intanto, la domanda americana ha superato le aspettative di Fiat, con numerosi concessionari che hanno già esaurito le prime assegnazioni.

Omologata negli USA, dove può circolare

La novità più significativa riguarda il riconoscimento della Topolino nella categoria statunitense dei Low-Speed Vehicles, veicoli a bassa velocità soggetti a requisiti specifici. L'omologazione consente di utilizzare la piccola Fiat sulle strade pubbliche, ma con limitazioni precise che dipendono anche dalle normative dei singoli Stati.La Topolino americana raggiunge una velocità massima di 40 km/h, equivalenti a 25 miglia orarie, e può circolare generalmente sulle strade con limiti non superiori a 56 km/h, ossia 35 miglia orarie. È inoltre possibile attraversare, dove consentito, arterie con limiti superiori, senza però percorrerle liberamente.Non si tratta quindi di un'automobile utilizzabile sulle autostrade o sulle principali arterie extraurbane. La sua destinazione rimane quella dei brevi trasferimenti locali, soprattutto nelle comunità residenziali, nelle località turistiche e nei centri urbani compatibili con questa categoria.

Arrivano la Open Air e due nuove colorazioni

L'aggiornamento della gamma statunitense introduce le tinte Corallo Orange e Luna Greige, affiancate da una nuova strumentazione digitale a colori. Cambia così la possibilità di personalizzare il quadriciclo, mantenendo le proporzioni compatte e l'impostazione essenziale che ne caratterizzano il progetto.La novità più interessante sul piano estetico è la Topolino Open Air, versione dotata di tetto apribile in tela. Una configurazione pensata soprattutto per i climi miti e le località costiere, dove la mobilità a cielo aperto rappresenta un'alternativa particolarmente interessante per i tragitti brevi. La risposta commerciale appare incoraggiante: diversi concessionari statunitensi hanno già esaurito le prime assegnazioni del modello 2026.

Fiat Topolino Sanlorenzo, l'esemplare unico ispirato agli yacht

Accanto alle novità destinate alla vendita, Fiat ha presentato al Fort Lauderdale International Boat Show una Topolino speciale sviluppata con Sanlorenzo, il cantiere italiano specializzato in yacht di lusso. Esposta a bordo di uno Sanlorenzo SX100, questa interpretazione unica trasferisce nell'abitacolo materiali e lavorazioni tipici della nautica. I sedili e la plancia adottano rivestimenti ricercati, mentre le cinture personalizzate e i dettagli in vera pelle sottolineano l'attenzione alle finiture.[gallery ids="293316,293317,293318,293319,293320,293321,293322"]L'elemento più caratteristico è il pavimento in legno naturale, ispirato ai ponti in teak delle imbarcazioni. Anche il tetto apribile partecipa alla reinterpretazione degli interni, creando un ambiente distante dalla semplicità del modello tradizionale.La collaborazione non annuncia una nuova versione commerciale, ma mostra le possibilità di personalizzazione della Topolino. Il modello, intanto, continua a ottenere risultati significativi in Europa: nei primi otto mesi del 2026 ha conquistato il 42,2% del mercato italiano dei quadricicli leggeri elettrici. Insomma, un piccolo ma concreto fenomeno.

items.content:
Hi everyone!

I had the idea for catcopter on my mind for a long time (got the domain ~13 years ago). It's a web multiplayer game where you can fly a dangerous cat and engage in competition with other players and critters (pterodactyls, chickens and angry penguins). I made it initially for me and my friends but it was quite fun so I thought I'll share it here too.

The game is intentionally dorky and it was fun to develop. The tools I used were mostly Opus 5.5 (objects / rigging / motion), Tripo3d for some elements I struggled with and Fable for optimisation (cpu / networking). Backend physics are done with Rapier. Luckily I had a lot of elements / game dynamics done before from another project of mine (https://flat.social) so the actual iteration here took me around a week.

items.title: Spotify prepara i remix con l'IA: il servizio (a pagamento) è previsto nel 2027
items.summary: Gli abbonati Premium potranno trasformare le canzoni degli artisti che aderiranno, creando remix e cover con l’IA ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Spotify starebbe preparando per l’inizio del 2027 il lancio del suo nuovo servizio basato sull’IA generativa, con il quale gli utenti potranno creare remix e cover partendo dalle canzoni presenti sulla piattaforma.

L’esistenza del progetto invece è ufficiale. Spotify lo aveva annunciato già a maggio insieme a Universal Music, spiegando che sarebbe stato proposto come funzione aggiuntiva a pagamento per gli utenti Premium e che avrebbe consentito di creare versioni alternative di brani degli artisti aderenti.

Spotify non vuole permettere di generare dal nulla una nuova canzone partendo da un prompt, ma di manipolare opere già esistenti e regolarmente concesse in licenza . Un utente potrebbe, per esempio, trasformare un brano folk in una versione dance oppure creare una cover che faccia interpretare una canzone nello stile vocale di un altro artista aderente al programma.

In ogni caso, gli artisti e gli autori dovranno scegliere se partecipare e riceveranno una quota del valore generato dalle nuove versioni delle proprie opere. La firma di un accordo con una casa discografica non significherà automaticamente che tutto il suo catalogo potrà essere manipolato dagli utenti. Gli artisti manterranno la possibilità di aderire oppure rifiutare individualmente il servizio.

Secondo il Financial Times, ottenere l’adesione delle star contemporanee si starebbe rivelando più difficile rispetto a quella di alcuni artisti con cataloghi più datati.

Universal Music è stato il primo grande partner ad annunciare pubblicamente un’intesa con Spotify, lo scorso maggio. In seguito sono arrivati gli accordi con Merlin, che rappresenta numerose etichette indipendenti; con Kobalt sul fronte dell’editoria musicale; e, più recentemente, con Believe e TuneCore.

Restano in corso, secondo il Financial Times, le trattative con Sony Music e Warner Music. Spotify non ritiene comunque indispensabile ottenere fin dall’inizio l’adesione di tutte le major: la società aveva già spiegato in estate che il servizio potrebbe essere lanciato con una selezione iniziale di artisti e cataloghi.

Secondo il piano attualmente allo studio, l’ascolto di un remix creato da un fan produrrebbe royalty anche per gli artisti e i detentori dei diritti del brano originale . Spotify sta lavorando affinché queste versioni possano entrare nelle playlist e affinché i relativi ascolti contribuiscano alle performance dell’opera originale nelle classifiche della piattaforma.

Inoltre, Spotify sostiene che ogni remix resterà collegato chiaramente alla canzone e all’artista di partenza , in modo che possa diventare anche uno strumento di scoperta dell’opera originale.

items.title: Femminicidi, più della metà degli orfani era presente al delitto
items.summary: Indagine del progetto Respiro su 124 orfani presi in carico in 6 regioni
items.content:
Più della metà aveva meno di nove anni quando è avvenuto il delitto, quasi uno su tre non ne aveva ancora compiuti sei. Nell'87,7 per cento dei casi documentati, l'autore del reato è un loro genitore e, al momento del delitto, più della metà dei bambini era in casa. Questa la fotografia degli orfani di femminicidio che emerge dall'indagine del progetto 'Respiro-Rete di sostegno per percorsi di inclusione e resilienza con gli orfani speciali', selezionato da Con i Bambini nell'ambito del fondo per il contrasto della povertà educativa minorile.

Il rapporto è stato presentato a Napoli in occasione dell'incontro 'Orfani di femminicidio: lo Stato che c'è. Cinque anni del progetto Respiro. La rilevazione raccoglie informazioni su 124 orfani, appartenenti a 78 nuclei familiari, presi in carico dal progetto in sei regioni: Basilicata, Calabria, Campania, Puglia, Sardegna e Sicilia.

Respiro è un progetto realizzato dalla cooperativa sociale Irene '95, capofila di una rete nazionale e territoriale che comprende Cismal, Save the Children Italia, Terre des Hommes Italia, Azienda ospedaliero-universitaria Policlinico di Bari-Giovanni XXIII, Centro Famiglie Catania, Cestrim onlus, Cipm Sardegna, Consorzio Co.Re, Progetto Sirio, Centro antiviolenza Thamaia, Koinos coop. sociale, Associazione Sinapsi.

items.title: Polymarket 1h halt after vendor compromise; affected users will be 'made whole'
items.summary: Article URL: https://www.nbcnews.com/business/consumer/polymarket-trading-halt-hack-wallets-rcna606405 Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50305225 Points: 87 # Comments: 31
items.content:
Prediction markets platform Polymarket was forced to halt trading on its international platform Thursday for nearly an hour because of what it said was a compromise of third-party software.

There were also unconfirmed reports from users on Polymarket’s Discord channel who said their wallets had been drained.

While Polymarket did not confirm that users had lost money, it said on X post “anyone who has been impacted will be made whole.”

“We’ll make this right and are fully reimbursing all affected traders,” the company said in a subsequent post on X .

Polymarket said the attack appeared to emanate from the United Kingdom and that it had referred the matter to British law enforcement authorities.

The hackers gained access to the funds via software from DebugBear, a web analytics and website performance tool, according to a person familiar with the details who was granted anonymity to address an evolving security situation.

DebugBear said on X that it was experiencing an “ongoing security incident” at around 2 p.m. ET Thursday.

Crypto news website The Block reported that some $2.65 million in cryptocurrencies had been siphoned from Polymarket users’ wallets, citing data from blockchain analysis group Arkham.

A Polymarket representative declined to comment on that figure or on the precise nature of the attack.

Polymarket said in its X post that it had identified and fixed an issue affecting its international platform, Polymarket.com.

“One of our 3rd party providers was compromised, and we have referred this to relevant law enforcement,” Polymarket said.

“Out of an abundance of caution, we have temporarily halted trading & are working to bring the platform back online,” it added.

Trading began again at 3 p.m. ET after nearly an hour offline.

Polymarket’s U.S.-based platform did not appear to be affected by the breach.

Compromising third-party vendors has become a common way malicious actors gain access to large platforms and websites.

These hackers’ success in stealing money from Polymarket users, however, makes this a significant breach.

Polymarket was valued at $21 billion in September after a group of investors led by Donald Trump Jr. invested $1 billion in the platform.

The company processes about $200 million worth of trading activity daily.

Polymarket, along with rival Kalshi, has become the subject of an intense, multimillion-dollar battle between U.S. states and the Trump administration over who gets to regulate the prediction-market betting that occurs on the sites.

The platforms also continue to fight off potential insider trading activity. Earlier Thursday, Bloomberg News reported Polymarket was investigating reports of suspicious bets made amid Israel’s closely watched elections.

It is also investigating “dozens” of bets related to the U.S. midterms, according to the company’s head of global intelligence and investigations, Shana Bautista.

Earlier this month, Kalshi said it was looking into suspicious bets involving Trump’s choice for press secretary.

Rob Wile is a Pulitzer Prize-winning journalist covering breaking business stories for NBCNews.com.

items.content:
tl;dr: Agents can play Pictionary. You can connect your own agent, or just watch a game in progress here: https://sketch.wakeshift.ai/games/q5ucru

Hi folks! I initially built this as a proof-of-concept for sending push notifications to AI agents. Watching the agents play Pictionary together has been compelling, so I thought I'd ship it as a standalone demonstration.

In Sketch Stadium, your agent subscribes to game events. Agents take turns either drawing or guessing. Easy clues are 1 point, medium are 2, and hard are 3. It's entertaining to watch and some of the drawings are impressive (and others are mind-bogglingly bad). This is the real opportunity for the model labs who have been pelican-maxxing to shine.

The first version gave agents the ability to draw lines 10 at a time so that it would be a little bit more like real Pictionary. However, it turns out agents are _really_ bad at drawing that way. So instead I let them use a subset of SVG to draw and that's worked much better, even for the lower-cost models.

You don't need to create an account to connect your agent, just add the MCP and authorize. But if you don't want to do that, just watch the game linked above.

As a bit more background, agents often start processes that take an indeterminate amount of time to complete (e.g. CI, waiting for approval in a separate system, sending an email and waiting for a reply). If an agent needs that process to complete before it can proceed, it can:

* poll,

* ask the user to tell it when it's done,

* use a bespoke built-in integration, or

* use a proprietary capability (e.g. Claude Code monitors)

Today, there's no easy, consistent way to wake up agents through a webhook or push notification. I dealt with this firsthand with Clawvisor (authorization for agents) where I needed agents to recognize when the operator had clicked an out-of-band approve button. The best-supported way to achieve that at the time was long-polling.

This project is basically a tech demo for Wakeshift, which is a cross-harness, simple SDK for providing push notifications for agents. It attaches to your MCP to allow consumers of your MCP to subscribe to real-time events, and uses whatever available hacks per harness to wake an agent when dormant. For most harnesses, Wakeshift requires a hook to be installed for the best experience. It will upgrade automatically as harnesses start adopting MCP events.

I'd love any feedback or ideas for other products or games that you'd want to see built on this capability. Or MCP servers that you use today that you think would benefit from push notifications.

items.title: Democratic senator blames Egypt press crackdown on US military aid decision
items.summary: Chris Murphy said waiving a human rights condition on aid paved the way for arrests of journalists.
items.content:
A top Democratic senator has blamed a crackdown on independent journalism in Egypt on a decision by the Trump administration to waive human rights conditions on US military funding to the country.

Chris Murphy, who sits on the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, accused the US government of "abandoning" the Egyptian people after it lifted restrictions relating to more than $300m of defence assistance.

Over the last month a series of arrests has taken place of journalists at two of the few remaining independent news outlets in Egypt, where newspapers and TV stations are closely controlled by the authorities.

The US State Department told the BBC it waived conditions on a portion of military aid to Egypt in September due to the country's "importance to US national security interests".

Murphy, speaking at the Middle East Institute (MEI) in Washington this week, said he was in no doubt the two were linked.

"The minute that money was released, the crackdown began in an absolutely devastating way," he said.

On Tuesday a court in Cairo ordered the closure of the news website Madr Masa and fined its editor-in-chief Lina Attalah in what Amnesty International called "a crushing blow to press freedom".

Earlier this month, authorities arrested six journalists at the independent fact-checking platform Matsda2sh and charged them with belonging to the outlawed Muslim Brotherhood.

The Egyptian Embassy in Washington did not respond to a request for comment.

Egyptian journalists from fact-checking website facing terrorism charges

TV presenter among 12 sentenced to death in Egypt drugs case

Cairo has remained a close regional ally of the US despite what human rights groups say are widespread abuses under President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi's government, including torture and enforced disappearances.

Sisi denies there are political prisoners in Egypt. He has previously said stability and security are paramount, adding authorities have promoted rights by trying to provide basic needs such as jobs and housing.

Washington sends Egypt £1.3bn ($1.73bn) per year, making it one of the world's biggest recipients of US military assistance.

US law allows up to £320m of the funding to be withheld, conditioned on Egypt meeting democracy and human rights requirements. But these restrictions can be waived by the administration on national security grounds.

In September, Secretary of State Marco Rubio waived human rights conditions on $320m of military aid in light of Egypt's role since the launch of the US war with Iran, according to a letter addressed to various Congressional committees. Egypt assisted negotiations between the US and Iran.

Exercising the waiver authority was "essential" for the US-Egypt relationship, "particularly in light of Egypt's helpful role following Operation Epic Fury," according to the September 4 memo seen by Reuters which bore Rubio's signature.

Asked by the BBC about the move in light of this month's arrests of journalists, the State Department said the waiver was "due to Egypt's importance to US national security interests, the concrete security cooperation Egypt provides to the United States, and the need to maintain that cooperation to address regional security challenges".

It added it maintained dialogue with Cairo on a "full range of issues" but would "not comment on private diplomatic conversations".

Rubio's move followed a similar decision by the Biden administration in 2024, when then Secretary of State Anthony Blinken waived human rights conditions to grant the full military aid allocation to Egypt as the US sought Cairo's role in mediating between Israel and Hamas in the war in Gaza.

Under Biden prior to 2024, the US withheld portions of the annual military allocation over Egypt's human rights record.

Murphy, who chairs a congressional committee on the Middle East and counterterrorism, said he had been a critic of both the Biden and Trump administrations over the issue.

"To the extent that there was any glimmer left of political speech in Egypt, it is gone for one proximate reason: The United States government abandoned the people of Egypt and decided to remove all conditions on our funding," Murphy told the MEI.

"Any hope of a true, meaningful political opposition rebirthing in Egypt has been shattered by this decision," he added.

US military aid to Cairo began after the 1978 Camp David Accords and the peace treaty that followed between Egypt and Israel. Successive administrations have viewed the world's most populous Arab country as a critical US ally in the region.

The group Reporters Without Borders describes Egypt , external as one of the world's biggest jailers of journalists.

The conviction of Lina Attalah and the closure of Madr Masr marked an unprecedented escalation in repression of press freedoms in Egypt, according to Timothy E Kaldas, Deputy Director of The Tahrir Institute for Middle East Policy, a Washington DC-based think tank.

He said both the US and European Union had been prioritising their strategic relations with Egypt over human rights and the rule of law in the country.

"It's been fostering a sense of impunity on the part of the Egyptian authorities that we're seeing play out," he told the BBC.

"Egypt is getting signals from both sides of the Atlantic that human rights and the rule of law are no longer a priority, and they're testing the limits of that."

He added: "The fact that they're not getting more robust pushback reinforces the wrong message."

  • Le barre di regolazione delle frequenze dell'equalizzatore risultano tagliate nella parte superiore dello schermo

  • Le app non riescono ad avviare nuove attività se aperte mentre è attiva una finestra in modalità Picture-in-Picture
  • Spaziatura irregolare tra le icone nella barra di stato

  • I pulsanti dell'interfaccia utente vengono visualizzati come quadrati bianchi vuoti, privi di icone, in modalità scura

  • Il dispositivo si blocca in modo intermittente nella schermata di blocco o subito dopo l'avvio

items.title: L'ordine dei medici: 'Dalla manovra risposte ancora insufficienti'
items.summary: '3,4 miliardi coprono i costi dell'energia, ma assunzioni, stipendi e liste di attesa restano senza risposta'
items.content:
"Risposte ancora insufficienti per personale e sanità territoriale". E' il giudizio del presidente della Federazione degli ordini dei medici (Fnomceo), Filippo Anelli, sulla manovra 2027. Le Regioni, rileva, "hanno chiesto 18 miliardi aggiuntivi per la sanità in tre anni. In realtà, nel 2027 arrivano 3,4 miliardi che copriranno sicuramente gli aumenti dei costi energetici, ma non consentiranno altri interventi, per esempio per la riduzione delle liste d'attesa. Anche assunzioni e stipendi restano senza risposta". Positivo invece, secondo Anelli, l'intervento sui fragili, ma a precise condizioni. "Sono tante le attese per una manovra finanziaria di rilancio del Servizio sanitario nazionale. Attese che, però, per le Regioni e per i professionisti, sono rimaste senza una risposta compiuta", sottolinea Anelli in un video per Fnomceo Tg Sanità. Il governo, osserva, "mette sul Fondo sanitario nazionale la cifra 'storica' di 146,3 miliardi per l'anno prossimo, ma i professionisti chiedevano un intervento straordinario per sbloccare le assunzioni e soprattutto allineare gli stipendi alla media europea".

Anche sul versante delle esigenze rappresentate dalle Regioni, le risorse, secondo il presidente, non consentono di rispondere pienamente alle necessità del servizio pubblico, a partire dallo sviluppo della sanità territoriale. Una apertura riguarda, invece, l'intervento a favore delle persone fragili. Per Anelli, queste risorse potrebbero infatti contribuire a rendere effettivo l'accesso alle prestazioni, soprattutto per chi incontra maggiori difficoltà economiche. A una condizione: che "vadano a implementare il fondo, già previsto dalla Legge, ma attualmente sottofinanziato, che permette di ricorrere alle prestazioni in intramoenia o nel privato quando le liste d'attesa sono troppo lunghe". E' "interessante - sottolinea - l'intervento sui fragili. Anche qui le risorse appostate potrebbero essere utilizzate in maniera adeguata se venisse finalmente applicata la Legge Prodi. Quel fondo - conclude Anelli - potrebbe, in questo modo, essere un utile strumento per andare incontro soprattutto alle persone più povere".

items.title: Israeli opposition accuses Netanyahu of trying to 'delegitimise' election
items.summary: The PM's Likud party has alleged foreign interference and said Arab-led parties "stole" the election after his coalition lost its majority.
items.content:
The main Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot and Arab-led party leaders have denounced Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for alleging foreign interference following the election which saw his coalition lose its majority.

Netanyahu's Likud accused Israel's Arab-led parties of "stealing" the election. Home security agency Shin Bet is investigating whether they received illegal funding from Qatar and Turkey.

Qatar's foreign ministry denied the "ridiculous and dangerous" allegations and accused Israeli politicians of conducting a disinformation campaign against Doha.

Final results confirmed that neither Netanyahu's bloc nor the Jewish opposition had won a majority in parliament.

The two Arab party lists - The Joint List and the Ra'am - defied expectations to win a record 19 seats in the 120-seat Knesset following a surge in turnout among Arab voters.

That positions them as potential kingmakers, with Netanyahu's bloc winning 53 seats and his rival Gadi Eisenkot's bloc securing 48.

According to protocol, the president will appoint a party leader whom he believes has the best chance to form a majority government. That leader has up to 42 days to achieve this, before the task passes to a second nominee who is given 28 days. If that nominee is unsuccessful, a period of 14 days is granted to a third candidate, after which, if no government has been formed, new elections will be called.

On Thursday Likud alleged that voters had been "bribed" to vote for Arab parties, after the head of the Central Elections Committee (CEC) asked the Shin Bet security service to investigate "serious suspicions" of foreign interference.

Both Arab parties strongly rejected the claim, with the Arab-majority Joint List alliance saying it was baseless.

The row is being seen by Netanyahu's critics as an attempt to delegitimise the Arab parties, thereby making it politically impossible for Eisenkot to join forces with them - which is currently his bloc's only route to power.

Israeli media reported that the CEC had been presented with a claim that Qatar had provided funding aimed at increasing voter turnout in Arab communities. Qatar's Foreign Ministry "categorically" denied the claims.

Netanyahu and his Likud Party framed the allegations as a "political earthquake" and an "an attack on democracy", aimed at removing their right-wing government.

But the Shin Bet later clarified that their investigation did not implicate an entire community who had voted legally, while acting CEC Director General Dean Livne said there was "no basis for allegations of systematic violations of election integrity."

Eisenkot, who was briefed on the investigation, said "it is too early to determine what happened, or if anything happened at all," and accused Netanyahu of running "an orchestrated and organized campaign to delegitimize the election results".

Balad chairman Sami Abu Shehadeh, who is part of the Joint List, dismissed the allegation, saying: "The losing side is constructing a racist blood libel and calling on the security agencies to use force in order to overturn the election results."

Netanyahu's attacks on Arab voters and parties have been ongoing for days. He spent much of election day posting on social media that high Arab turnout is an "emergency" and a "matter of life or death" for the Israeli right. He also shared AI-generated images of Arab voters at polling stations, in an attempt to encourage right-wingers to get out and vote.

Arab Israelis, many of whom refer to themselves as Palestinian citizens of Israel, make up about one fifth of the country.

For years, many boycotted Israeli elections, saying voting would legitimise a system that they say treats them as second-class citizens. But their turnout on Tuesday was inspired by a desire to oust the most right-wing governing coalition in Israel's history, led by Netanyahu.

The final results offer only three plausible options for a government to be formed: a national unity government involving Netanyahu and Eisenkot, a right-wing coalition involving Netanyahu and defectors from Eisenkot's bloc, or an Eisenkot-led government supported by the Arab parties.

Eisenkot and every member of his bloc bar one has previously refused to enter government with Arab parties, but speculation has swirled in recent days that an agreement could yet be reached.

A snap poll conducted by Hebrew University showed that the most popular option for voters from every party in the opposition bloc was for Eisenkot to form a minority government with Ra'am, and supported from outside by the Joint List.

items.title: Six dead after helicopter crashes in northern Indian state
items.summary: The aircraft reportedly took off from the Hindu pilgrimage site of Badrinath on Friday afternoon before losing contact.
items.content:
Five pilgrims and a pilot have died after their helicopter crashed in the northern Indian state of Uttarakhand, officials say.

The aircraft reportedly took off from the Hindu pilgrimage site of Badrinath on Friday afternoon before losing contact.

The cause of the crash is not yet known but there had been reports of heavy rain and poor visibility in the region.

Uttarakhand, a Himalayan state which borders China and Nepal, is home to some of Hinduism's holiest shrines and attracts millions of pilgrims every year.

Badrinath is one of four sacred sites on the Char Dham pilgrimage circuit, alongside Kedarnath, Gangotri and Yamunotri. Many devotees travel through steep Himalayan valleys to reach the temples, which are open for only part of the year because of harsh winter conditions.

Uttarakhand's Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami said the helicopter came down near a village close to Joshimath in Chamoli district.

The local civil aviation authority later confirmed to Indian media that six bodies had been located.

Helicopter services have become increasingly popular among pilgrims seeking to avoid difficult mountain journeys, but their safety has come under scrutiny following a series of accidents.

Before Friday's crash, India's weather department had issued an orange alert for the area, warning of thunderstorms, hail and strong winds.

In June 2025 , seven people were killed when a helicopter carrying pilgrims crashed near Kedarnath. Another seven died in a crash on the same pilgrimage route in October 2022.

Several other helicopter accidents were reported during the 2025 pilgrimage season, prompting aviation authorities to tighten safety checks and restrict some operations.
